concepts.label: Exact-cut qualification
concepts.definition: Evaluation bound to an exact immutable cut and member set, exact claim bytes, governing Product/release basis, each property's observation boundary, evidence subjects, owner verdicts, gaps and complete successor relation.

grounding.quote:
A Product authority may declare an explicit cross-Product Release-Matched
Asset Cohort when one source corpus and its required distributed or
derived assets need to remain usable as one versioned set. The declaring
relation names every required Product and asset, the exact source
dependency, its owning authorities, the qualification boundary and the
publication transaction. Path co-location, equal version text or a common
actor cannot infer the relation (P3, P6).

concepts.label: Release-Matched Asset Cohort
concepts.definition: Cross-Product Release-Matched Asset Cohort naming every required Product and asset, exact source dependency, owning authorities, qualification boundary and publication transaction. The STDO stack cohort contains the exact standards cut, its distributed spec plugin/host assets, exact Axiom Indexer mechanics Product, exact STDO Representation Product, and its released a_c.STDO program/logical constraint map or equivalent semantic index with complete source member inventory, member digests, member-set digest and exact derivation cut.
conditions: A Product authority explicitly declares the relation when a source corpus and required distributed or derived assets need to be usable as one versioned set.

concepts.label: Successor semantic disposition
concepts.definition: One semantic claim about that predecessor claim: conserved means retained; superseded means replaced by an accepted successor relation; intentionally removed means removed by current Product authority; not applicable means no successor effect with bounded reason. These are predicates to evaluate, not core result values or the decision owner's acceptance disposition. Unresolved states no claim and has no result.
conditions: A predecessor claim is capable of affecting the successor.

grounding.quote:
the table traces that section in its first two rows, whose rule column
names it, and owns none of it. Each commitment's standing is written as
the table of commitments in FOUNDATIONS §3 states it.

concepts.label: F15 release and successor conservation
concepts.definition: F15 traces release and successor-conservation laws from commitments plus explicitly additional instance premises: recursive products, published cuts, mutable carriers, derived assets, external services and successor lines. It traces but does not own FOUNDATIONS lineage objects. P1/P3/P6 are cited as independent, P0 as recovered, P4b as derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts, and P5 as derived from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. Domain choices and their owners are distinct from consequences.

grounding.quote:
It is realised from [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md),
[REFERENCE_FRAME](REFERENCE_FRAME.md), [ACTIVATION](ACTIVATION.md) and
[EVALUATION](EVALUATION.md): nothing here is foundational, every clause
names the principle that requires it (P0 to P6, FOUNDATIONS §3), and each
mechanism could be realised differently under the same principles.

concepts.label: SPEC_METHOD
concepts.definition: Tier-2 particular method owning position/identity, constitutional chain and surfaces, manifesto/litmus tests, requirement/design/trace/live-surface laws, outcome conservation, change management/triage/classification/consistency/sprint boundaries, ambiguity/lifecycle, lineage/release boundary, migration/procedures/design records and build-tenant binding. It is a realisation of FOUNDATIONS, REFERENCE_FRAME, ACTIVATION and EVALUATION, not itself foundational; other Tier-2 members own project binding, testing, work carriers and release mechanics.

grounding.quote:
Its role is meta-constitutional: it defines how goals, intent, product,
requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing relate; what counts as
specification sufficiency; what kinds of requirement truth exist; and how
authority flows during iterative delivery. If a project's implementation
disappears, the method should still be sufficient to bootstrap a new
spec-driven project process from scratch; the method plus the surviving domain specification
can reconstruct the project (P2, P0).

concepts.label: Process constitution
concepts.definition: Meta-constitutional process for spec-driven projects defining relations among goals, intent, product, requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing; specification sufficiency; kinds of requirement truth; and authority during iterative delivery. The method should bootstrap a new process if implementation disappears; method plus surviving domain specification can reconstruct the project.

grounding.quote:
S,
Specification, owned by this member; T, Ticketing, owned by
[TICKETS](TICKETS.md); D, Design, owned by the design profile member
[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md); and O, Outcome-Driven Development, the
complete area whose identity and realisation meaning are owned by its
profile member [ODD](ODD.md).

concepts.label: STDO method identity
concepts.definition: STDO names four method-law areas: S Specification owned by SPEC_METHOD; T Ticketing owned by TICKETS; D Design owned by DESIGN_MODULE; O Outcome-Driven Development, whose complete identity and realisation meaning are owned by ODD.
conditions: Within urn:stdo:bounded-context:method-identity under the selected complete basis.

grounding.quote:
Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code
  → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis
  → Repricing at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Constitutional chain
concepts.definition: Homeostatic responsibility chain: Goals → Intent → Product Definition → Requirements → Design → Code → Events → Projection → Delta → Scenarios → Gap analysis → Repricing at the layer named by change class. Goals name current work-wave concerns; intent purpose/direction; Product Definition the current mutable source project's terms, boundaries and end-state shape; requirements invariant obligations; design structural decisions/interfaces/carriers/topology; Code realisation in software, human procedure or both; Events retained happenings; Projection reconstructs current truth from sufficient retained records; Delta exposes intended/realised drift; Scenarios test operational meaning; Gap analysis finds model insufficiency; Repricing changes the appropriate layer and generates new goals/intent when work-wave, direction or scope changes.

grounding.quote:
Standing of the commitments cited (FOUNDATIONS §3): P0
recovered; P1, P2, P3, P4a and P6 independent; P4b derived from P0 and
P2, with P0's premise that step-produced facts are not re-acquirable; P5
derived from P0 and P6, with P0's open-world premise.

concepts.label: F10 chain, outcome and build-tenant binding
concepts.definition: F10 traces how specification governs realisations from owned layers, layered surfaces, several changing realisations and immutable releases as instance premises not supplied by commitments. Commitment standings are P0 recovered; P1/P2/P3/P4a/P6 independent; P4b derived from P0/P2 with non-reacquirable step-produced facts; P5 derived from P0/P6 with the open-world premise. It distinguishes consequences, owning rules, domain/policy choices and consumers.

grounding.quote:
The method commits to these (P2, P6). It defines the
current goals for the active body of work before repricing deeper
constitutional layers. It works from intent before implementation. It
defines the current product definition in explicit present-tense terms
before decomposing it into detailed requirements. It defines the full
constitutional what in requirements, not merely a feature list. It prefers
declaring desired truth and lawful boundaries over prescribing step-by-step
imperative procedure. It makes design the explicit structural bridge
between requirements and code. It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent. It treats
spec-driven development as a disambiguation pipeline: each major gate
reduces the space of lawful interpretations before downstream realisation
proceeds.

concepts.label: Specification-driven method
concepts.definition: Specification-driven development is a governed derivation and disambiguation method: current goals precede deeper repricing, intent precedes implementation, product definition precedes detailed requirements, and design explicitly bridges requirements to code.

grounding.quote:
Goals orient the current bounded work
wave and are not a substitute requirement surface.

concepts.label: Goals surface
concepts.definition: Goals orient the current bounded work wave; they do not substitute for requirements.

grounding.quote:
Intent states why the
system exists and what directional change is in or out of scope; it carries
no optional realisation detail unless that detail is itself constitutional.

concepts.label: Intent surface
concepts.definition: Intent states why the system exists and which directional change is in or out of scope.

grounding.quote:
Product states the current concrete product definition and bridges intent
to requirements; it is not a release-note surface; it carries enough
operational lifecycle signal for downstream requirements and design to
understand intended use, release and install posture, live-use posture,
observability posture, and retirement or supersession posture where those
materially affect product meaning.

concepts.label: Product definition
concepts.definition: Product definition is the current concrete, present-tense bridge from intent to requirements, including lifecycle signal material to product meaning; it is not release notes.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state stable obligations
that must be true; they carry explicit acceptance criteria and remain
sufficient for downstream design derivation, including lifecycle
obligations or named lifecycle ambiguity gaps where build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, telemetry or retirement materially affect
the obligation.

concepts.label: Requirements surface
concepts.definition: Requirements state the full constitutional WHAT as stable obligations with explicit acceptance criteria, sufficient for downstream design derivation.

grounding.quote:
Design states how requirement truth is realised; it is
downstream of requirements and may choose structure, interfaces, carriers,
packaging and tenant boundaries. ADRs are durable design memory, not a
second requirement surface.

concepts.label: Design surface
concepts.definition: Design is the downstream structural HOW that realises requirement truth and chooses lawful mechanisms, structures, interfaces, carriers, packaging and tenant boundaries.

grounding.quote:
It requires code to be derivable from
requirements and design, not defended as accidental precedent.

concepts.label: Code realisation
concepts.definition: Code is executable realisation derived from requirements and design, rather than a source of authority through accidental precedent.

grounding.quote:
The generic law, that a layered specification is sufficient when a competent
actor can derive each layer from the one above, that sufficiency is not
determinism, that a boundary crossed only by hiding a major ambiguity is not
sufficient, and that an accepted relation may be reused on its exact basis
after checking applicability and invalidation, is EVALUATION §6.

concepts.label: Reconstruction sufficiency
concepts.definition: Reconstruction sufficiency is competent reconstruction of conformant downstream layers in order. It is not determinism and cannot depend on hiding major ambiguity.

grounding.quote: current specification → real-world use case → gap analysis → re-entry at the layer its change class names

concepts.label: Renewal cycle
concepts.definition: Renewal is the cumulative feedback cycle from current specification through real-world use case and explicit gap analysis to lawful re-entry and forward repricing.

grounding.quote:
For a realisation boundary that the design profile governs (DESIGN_MODULE,
tier 3, adopted under its own adoption rule), the core rule is: semantic
steps should read as transforms over admitted truth; effects should be
explicit and pushed to the edge. If a reader has to inspect orchestration
code, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults to
determine what the system means, the design is too imperative and too
coupled (P1, P6).

concepts.label: Profile-governed realisation shape
concepts.definition: The design profile's realisation shape makes meaning readable as transforms over admitted truth and locates effects explicitly at the edge.
conditions: The tier-3 DESIGN_MODULE profile governs the boundary under its own adoption rule.

grounding.quote:
| Capability | a behaviour, function or surface the system must provide | what can the system do |
| Constraint / Guarantee | an invariant, law, safety property, portability rule or semantic guarantee that bounds how the system may behave | what must always remain true |
| Governance | a policy or control rule over lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator action | what governs use and change |
| Verification | a requirement on tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic surfaces | how do we know the claim is true |

Every live requirement family is classified on two independent axes (P3,
P1): lifecycle status (Active,
Deferred, Superseded, Orphaned) and requirement category (the four above).

concepts.label: Requirement classifications
concepts.definition: Requirement category and lifecycle status are independent declared-state domains. Categories are Capability (required behaviour/function/surface), Constraint / Guarantee (invariant, law, safety, portability or semantic bound), Governance (lifecycle, authority, visibility, release or operator policy), and Verification (tests, evidence, traceability, qualification or forensic obligations). Statuses are Active, Deferred, Superseded and Orphaned.

grounding.quote:
Spec-driven development requires constitutional trace closure: the rule
that closes the constitution over realised behaviour, stricter than
documentation completeness (P6, P4b).

concepts.label: Constitutional trace closure
concepts.definition: Constitutional trace closure closes the constitution over realised behaviour and is stricter than documentation completeness.

grounding.quote:
A project may accumulate multiple live domain surfaces over time. A live
surface is versioned constitutional history, not scratch space (P3). Engine code, design documents, tests and
tooling may be refactored aggressively while they remain mutable
implementation surfaces. Live domain artifacts, once published as live
constitutional surfaces, are immutable in place; if one is wrong, the valid
actions are to supersede it with a new version or to withdraw or delete it

concepts.label: Live domain surface
concepts.definition: A live domain surface is versioned constitutional history, immutable in place; a project may accumulate multiple such surfaces.
conditions: A domain artifact has been published as a live constitutional surface.

grounding.quote:
Any material
product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin
surface, public interface, data surface or capability has an operational
lifecycle, whose canonical chain is intent, requirement, build, assurance,
release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry, retirement.

Each phase has one of three answers, and this
section owns them: the phase is answered by the surface; if a phase is
not applicable, the surface says why; if it is unknown, a named gap such
as `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` is recorded.
Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.

concepts.label: Operational lifecycle
concepts.definition: The canonical operational lifecycle is intent, requirement, build, assurance, release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry and retirement. A phase has one declared answer: answered; not applicable with reason; or a named Gap:/Unanswered: marker.
conditions: The designed product, application, module, function, runtime surface, plugin surface, public interface, data surface or capability is material.

grounding.quote:
Qualification evaluates each
disposition on evidence and records a value of the core result algebra
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) with that predicate.
An unresolved disposition states no claim and so has no result: in the
qualification of the affected claim it is a planned assessment without a
closed result, which is why it blocks that qualification

relations.meaning: Qualification evaluates the semantic disposition predicate and records its core value; the disposition label is not itself the result.
conditions: A semantic disposition is asserted and evaluated on evidence.
exceptions: An unresolved disposition states no claim and has no result.

grounding.quote:
Its role is meta-constitutional: it defines how goals, intent, product,
requirements, design, code, evidence and repricing relate; what counts as
specification sufficiency; what kinds of requirement truth exist; and how
authority flows during iterative delivery.

relations.meaning: The source explicitly assigns the process constitution authority to define relations and sufficiency across the constitutional chain; it does not replace project-domain WHAT.
conditions: A project follows the described spec-driven process.

grounding.quote:
goals govern intent, intent governs
product definition

conditions: Throughout iteration.

grounding.quote:
intent governs
product definition

conditions: Throughout iteration.

grounding.quote: product definition governs requirements

conditions: Throughout iteration.

grounding.quote:
requirements
govern design

conditions: Throughout iteration.

grounding.quote: requirements plus design govern code.

relations.meaning: Requirements and design jointly govern code; this edge does not grant requirements-only sufficiency.
conditions: Jointly with design; throughout iteration.

grounding.quote: requirements plus design govern code.

relations.meaning: Design and requirements jointly govern code; this edge does not grant design-only authority.
conditions: Jointly with requirements; throughout iteration.

grounding.quote:
The cohort is incomplete when a required member is missing, stale,
differently versioned, built from another source cut, or unable to
reproduce its declared source-member and digest closure. A change to any
source member covered by the index invalidates the old derived candidate
for the successor cohort. The index is regenerated, mechanically
validated, independently qualified where required, and released under the
same new cut name. A stale index may remain immutable history; it cannot
accompany the changed source as the current cohort (P3, P5, P6).

constraints.statement: Every required member uses exact <version>-rc.<n> suffix: cut/ref rendering adds v, embedded asset version does not. Qualification normalises only this leading marker and requires exact suffix equality. Equality establishes matching only, never Product/member/tag/acceptance/authority identity. Missing, stale, differently versioned, other-source-cut or nonreproducible source-member/digest closure makes cohort incomplete. Any covered source-member change invalidates old derived candidate for successor; regenerate, mechanically validate, independently qualify where required and release index under same new cut name.
conditions: A cohort is explicitly declared.
exceptions: A stale derived index may remain immutable history, but not accompany changed source as current cohort.

grounding.quote:
If the remote does not support atomic ref publication, publication
refuses. The process has no sequential-push fallback. Every immutable cut
tag is create-only and therefore requires bound remote absence. Every
mutable carrier, RC branch, selector and release branch uses an explicit
per-ref compare-and-swap lease, such as
`--force-with-lease=<ref>:<expected-oid>`, in that same atomic
transaction. A missing expected ref, unexpected existing tag or changed
remote object ID stops publication; the operator refetches and repeats
complete content and local-ref-graph qualification before constructing
another push. A lease mismatch never falls back to an unguarded force, a
partial push or an in-place expectation update (P5, P3).

constraints.statement: Refuse remote lacking atomic publication; no sequential fallback. Immutable tags are create-only with bound remote absence. Every mutable carrier/RC/selector/release ref uses explicit per-ref compare-and-swap lease in same atomic transaction. Missing expected ref, unexpected tag or changed OID stops publication; refetch and repeat full content/local-ref-graph qualification before another push. Never substitute unguarded force, partial push or in-place expectation update. Remote verification fails closed for any required ref absent, lightweight, differently versioned, wrong Product commit or selector/release-branch mismatch.
conditions: Publishing or remotely verifying a coordinated cohort.
exceptions: Later bookkeeping commits are allowed without moving immutable cohort tags.

grounding.quote:
A historically published source cut may be the basis of a later
same-version backfill only when separately authorised recovery law names
that exception. Every recovered asset still binds the exact historical cut
and same cut name, and remote completeness remains mandatory. Recovery
cannot move the historical tag, add bytes to its Product subject, or be
represented as an atomic cohort that existed at the original publication.
Normal successor publication uses the atomic cohort process above (P3,
P6).

constraints.statement: Content qualification binds exact A tag/manifest, B source tree, all Product target refs/version markers/inventories/index bytes/full source digest closure, establishing tagging requires no qualifying-byte change. After refs exist, local-ref qualification binds annotated objects, peels, targets, exact push set and all remote expectations/absences to unchanged content result. Post-publication verifies same relation remotely and refuses partial cohort. Authorised backfill must retain exact historical cut/name and complete remote set; it cannot move tag, add Product bytes or claim original atomic existence. Normal successors use atomic process. Adding/changing cohort law changes qualifying bytes and governs only a higher RC containing them, never retroactively an earlier cut.
constraints.uncertainty: No separate recovery law is supplied.
conditions: Cohort qualification, recovery or change to cohort law.
exceptions: Historical same-version backfill only under separately authorised recovery law naming that exception.

grounding.quote:
A clean skip caused by an unhealthy external dependency is an evaluation
not performed, which has no result
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), Not performed). It may
preserve correct Product classification, but it cannot establish that the
dependent capability passed. The claim is either qualified against a
healthy dependency or narrowed before acceptance (P6, P5).

constraints.statement: A dependency may remain outside Product for carrier/migration classification and still block dependent claim. A clean skip due to unhealthy dependency is unperformed evaluation with no result; correct classification does not establish capability passed. Qualify with healthy dependency or narrow claim before acceptance.
conditions: A release claim depends on an external backend, transport or operator-facing service.
exceptions: The claim may be narrowed before acceptance instead of qualified against a healthy dependency.

grounding.quote:
an obligation stays obligatory, a preference
stays a preference, and every permitted exception and scope condition
survives, or the claim is not conserved. A statement that a whole
package's wording is equivalent establishes none of this for any claim
(P6, P1). A `conserved` disposition recorded
before this test applied is re-evaluated under it before the affected
claim qualifies; until then its standing is `unresolved`.

constraints.statement: Identify exact immutable predecessor; origin remains fixed for candidate. Every potentially affecting predecessor claim receives one semantic disposition. Retain/reassess evidence under change-impact law. Conservation compares same material case, scope and authority, must/may/prohibited outcomes, absent triggers/exceptions/prerequisites, owning text and consumer bindings, with discriminating counterexamples. Patch absence is not loss if successor-native behaviour is preserved; naming/code similarity is not conservation evidence. Indicative wording can bind; replacing must/shall alone neither conserves nor supersedes. Preserve obligation/preference force and every exception/scope condition. Package-wide equivalence proves no individual claim. Earlier conserved records predating this test must be reevaluated before qualification, remaining unresolved until then. Unresolved disposition blocks affected-claim qualification as a planned assessment without closed result; qualification records core value with each asserted disposition predicate, never treats disposition label as result.
conditions: A successor evolves predecessor semantic claims.
exceptions: Earlier conserved evidence may be reused when owning text and carrying consumer bindings are unchanged or the change demonstrably does not affect the claim.

grounding.quote:
Its
overriding bias is declarative rather than imperative: the system should
primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence
surfaces, and let lawful processing derive and realise work from that
declared surface.
Imperative procedure still exists and is subordinate to declared authority
(P6, P1).

constraints.statement: Treat specification as constitutional source, enabling re-derivation, audit and correction under explicit authority. Declarative bias is a should: primarily declare truths, structures, interfaces, constraints and evidence surfaces for lawful derivation/realisation. Imperative procedure remains subordinate to declared authority. Constitutional examples use neutral capability/authority identities to demonstrate capabilities; consumer particulars are not precedent that becomes method law.

grounding.quote:
The authoritative split is strict: the surfaces bound as WHAT define WHAT;
design and realisation surfaces define HOW; no build tenant, design, code,
definition overlay or derived surface becomes co-equal constitutional
authority with the bound WHAT (P6).

constraints.statement: Method owns process constitution; goals current overriding work concerns; intent domain direction; product-definition current mutable source-project definition; requirements live obligations derived from it; shared/tenant-local design concrete mechanisms. Product definition binds actual authority locations and tenant registry realisations under shared specification. Bound WHAT alone defines WHAT; design/realisation define HOW. Tenants, design, code, definition overlays and derived surfaces never become co-equal with WHAT. Conventional GOALS.md, INTENT.md, PRODUCT.md and specification/requirements/ require no relocation/duplication. Structured requirement families are preferred to an imperative monolithic catch-all; location itself is not constitutional.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed binding and registry laws are external.

grounding.quote:
The expansion does not make the four owning
members independently selectable and does not reduce the released product
to four members: consumer authority remains one complete immutable released
cut with its exact member inventory ([RELEASE](RELEASE.md)).

constraints.statement: Four named areas do not make their owning members independently selectable or reduce the released Product to four members. Consumer authority remains one complete immutable released cut with exact member inventory.

grounding.quote:
The lifecycle is a governed disambiguation pipeline: each major
boundary reduces the space of lawful interpretations and surfaces major
ambiguity explicitly; detection is mandatory; blocking or escalation is
policy under declared risk appetite, except for hard-stop prerequisite
failures (§5; ACTIVATION §4).

constraints.statement: The canonical statement routes each clause to its owner and decides nothing independently. Every Product publishes a layout-neutral routing definition locating constitution/local decisions/collective frame bases/WHAT/independent tenant HOW/work/composition, not rival truth. Material terms resolve under bounded context, owner, selected basis and scope; spelling creates no cross-context meaning/authority; explicit imports/translations/equivalences/disambiguations govern seams; zero or multiple applicable meanings fail closed. Requirements cover capabilities, guarantees, governance and verification; design records structural HOW. Major boundaries reduce lawful interpretations and explicitly detect ambiguity. Implementations never replace constitution. Scenarios supply end-to-end proof where capability claims need it. Design derives from requirements, requirements from goals/intent/product, code from requirements/design. Iteration cumulatively reprices; events/projection/delta reveal drift. Every live requirement family has design ownership, classification and downstream closure or explicit deferment; every design record grounds in requirements; shipping behaviour traces authority. Live surfaces change through supersession/withdrawal, never silent mutation. New intent follows real cases and gap analysis. Sprints price proof cost and force close review; they are no authority layer or concealment of drift.
constraints.uncertainty: Several owning sections and hard-stop definitions are not supplied.
exceptions: Ambiguity blocking/escalation is policy under declared risk appetite except hard-stop prerequisite failures.

grounding.quote: A realisation choice that no upper layer constrains belongs to design.

constraints.statement: Declared specification governs; realisations/overlays/views realise, locate or project without co-equal authority. Each live requirement needs owning design decision and downstream closure or explicit deferment; behaviour traces authorising requirements/design and broken trace is drift. A layer is sufficient when a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer; derivation failure is an upper-layer defect. Unconstrained realisation choice belongs to design. Live constitutional surfaces are versioned history changed through supersession/withdrawal, never in place; current truth uses present tense, not version labels denoting recency. Use-exposed inexpressible constitutional conditions reprice the deficient surface or remain recorded governed debt; unanswered lifecycle phases remain recorded gaps. F10 identifies requirement categories/statuses, ADR fields/lifecycle/storage, Gap:/Unanswered: markers and conventional chain layout as domain choices, not consequences supplied by commitments alone.
constraints.uncertainty: Exact category/status values and detailed ADR/lifecycle rules are outside this excerpt.
conditions: Applying F10's owned-layer, layered-surface and realisation premises.
exceptions: Explicit deferment may substitute for downstream closure.
Multiple conformant realisations may satisfy a layer.
Explicit version labels may identify immutable release facts, selectors or clearly historical/superseded material.

grounding.quote: A regression or unresolved gap falsifies the claim of the path it affects, so it blocks further promotion only on that path.

constraints.statement: Progress is judged against one selected directly verifiable outcome per work wave; evidence evaluates but cannot select/enlarge/replace outcome. Growth requires admitted basis and ends with it; regression/unresolved gap blocks promotion only on affected path. Closure evidence includes authority trace, realisation proof, negative proof where drift plausible, and remaining open pressure, under external TICKETS/EVALUATION/ASSURANCE laws. Lineage objects remain distinct and consumers select one complete release; reusable method change retains one authority relation from evidence to realising consumer. Method terms resolve in declared bounded context. Under governing design profile, semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth with explicit edge effects; higher-order/effectful boundaries require explicit composition/effect algebra without mandatory vocabulary. Admission carriers, evidence categories, eight-step adoption chain and mechanics are expressly allocated policy/domain choices.
constraints.uncertainty: Full progress categories, growth admission, adoption chain and design-profile rules are external.
conditions: Evaluating progress, closure, lineage or realisation shape under F10.
exceptions: Negative proof is needed where drift is plausible.
Realisation-shape recommendations are scoped to boundaries governed by the design profile.

grounding.quote: Only an obligation's owner can weaken it (P6), so a change that needs a weaker obligation is a change to the WHAT at its owning layer.

constraints.statement: Different means may realise the same obligations; obligations decide fitness. Executor kind neither accepts nor rejects a realisation, human performance is not adjudication, convenient stack weakens nothing, and structural representation validation does not prove correct execution. Binding divides requirements calculus, computational calculus and execution environment, chosen as tenant design. Identify operations, outcome values mapped to core, resource measures/units/boundaries and obligation-required limits so finite actors can evaluate them. Calculus may serve wherever its laws hold regardless of executor. Multi-tenant development mechanics belong to project law. Construction steps, data meaning and execution remain three separate accounts; mappings state and discharge preservation under ACTIVATION Refinement and AC-013 when recorded in a_c, with joined accounts and environmental evidence owned by tenant binding.
constraints.uncertainty: Full §11, resource-limit law and three-account definitions are not supplied.
conditions: A build tenant binds obligations to a realisation.
exceptions: Only an obligation's owner can weaken it by changing WHAT at its owning layer.

grounding.quote:
This is the homeostatic loop. Every link is load-bearing. A break at any
link, goals with no downstream repricing path, an unowned requirement, an
ungrounded design record, code without a design decision, creates
accidental law (P6). Load-bearing means owned, not software: the links
Code, Events and Projection name responsibilities every realisation
carries in the carrier its binding selects (§11), and no product owes a
code base or an event store that its binding does not select (P2, P6).

constraints.statement: Every chain link is owned and load-bearing; absent repricing path, unowned requirement, ungrounded design or code without design decision creates accidental law. ADR is a durable design record, not another constitutional layer. Code/Events/Projection are binding-selected responsibilities across software/human/mixed realisations, not universal codebase/event-store requirements. Goals keep temporary work focus out of deeper layers until intentional repricing. Present-tense Product Definition bridges direction to requirements, naming source-project terms/boundaries; it is neither immutable cut nor installed Product. Requirements state mandatory truth including capabilities/invariants/constraints/governance/verification, not merely visible features. Design chooses mechanisms, interfaces/topology/placement/carriers/entry-control/runtime wiring/lawful tenant boundaries; requirements may mandate delivered surfaces without deciding placement unless path is constitutional. Constitutional insufficiency re-enters at change-class-named layer.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed change classes and §11 binding rules are only referenced.
exceptions: Projection need not replay a complete event stream if retained record is sufficient for Product obligations.
Design chooses where/how required surfaces are realised unless the path itself is constitutional.

grounding.quote:
It demands evidence for claims through scenarios, tests, events,
projection and delta. It treats repricing as part of correctness: when
reality exposes a constitutional gap, the specification changes. It keeps
authority directional while iterating: goals govern intent, intent governs
product definition, product definition governs requirements, requirements
govern design, and requirements plus design govern code. It keeps the live
operative surface in the present tense only: once a new current reality is
established, transitional paths are erased from the live product unless
explicitly retained as compatibility features. It treats derived artifacts,
indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views, as read
models, never as constitutional truth. If these claims do not hold, the
work is not spec-driven.

constraints.statement: The method requires full constitutional requirements, code derivable from requirements/design, narrowing at major gates, evidence through scenarios/tests/events/projection/delta, and specification repricing when reality exposes a constitutional gap. Authority stays directional during iteration. Current operative truth is present-tense; obsolete transitions are erased subject to the compatibility exception. Derived artifacts, indexes, trace matrices, reports, automation and generated views are read models, never constitutional truth. Failure of these commitments excludes the spec-driven designation. Declarative truth/boundaries over imperative procedure remains a preference.
exceptions: Transitional paths may remain as explicitly retained compatibility features.

grounding.quote:
The work is not spec-driven if any of these holds (P2, P6):

1. Given goals, a competent team cannot derive a conformant intent surface.
2. Given intent, a competent team cannot derive a conformant
   product-definition surface.
3. Given product definition, a competent team cannot derive conformant
   requirements.
4. Given requirements, a competent team cannot derive a conformant design.
5. Given requirements and design, a competent team cannot derive conformant
   code.
6. A live requirement has no explicit status, category or owning design
   decision.
7. A live requirement has no downstream realisation or explicit deferment
   surface.
8. Code behaviour exists without requirement and design authority.
9. A live domain artifact is rewritten in place after becoming part of the
   live constitutional surface.
10. A capability claim has no operational evidence.
11. Drift is discovered, [Universal intake triage](#universal-intake-triage)
    locates its cause in the constitutional source, and that source is not
    repriced.
12. A major ambiguity at a constitutional or realisation boundary is neither
    recorded nor explicitly governed.
13. A material product, module, function, application, runtime surface or
    capability has no declared operational lifecycle signal and no recorded
    gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or
    retirement questions.

constraints.statement: Work is not spec-driven if a competent team cannot derive conformant intent from goals, product definition from intent, requirements from product, design from requirements, or code from requirements plus design; if any live requirement lacks explicit status, category, owning design decision, or both downstream realisation and explicit deferment; if code lacks requirement/design authority; if a live constitutional domain artifact is rewritten in place; if a capability lacks operational evidence; if triage attributes discovered drift to constitutional source that is not repriced; if major boundary ambiguity is neither recorded nor explicitly governed; or if a material product/module/function/application/runtime surface/capability has neither declared lifecycle signal nor recorded gap for unanswered release, deployment, live-use, telemetry or retirement questions.
constraints.uncertainty: These are exclusion conditions, not an independently sufficient acceptance test.
conditions: Any listed failure holds.

grounding.quote:
A failure at any boundary is a specification defect of the upper layer. If
intent cannot be derived from goals, the goals surface is unclear,
contradictory or not concrete enough to orient the next bounded wave of
work. If product cannot be derived from intent, the intent surface is too
vague, contradictory or not concrete enough to guide realisation. If
requirements cannot be derived from product, the product surface is
underspecified, contradictory or not decomposable enough to govern
implementation. If design cannot be derived from requirements, the
requirement surface is underspecified, contradictory or polluted with
accidental implementation detail. If code cannot be derived from
requirements plus design, the design surface is incomplete, ambiguous or
not operational enough. ADRs and design documents are therefore not
decorative explanation; they are the load-bearing bridge between
constitutional truth and executable realisation.

constraints.statement: Specification-drivenness requires ordered reconstructability. Boundary failure is an upper-layer defect: goals unclear/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for the bounded wave; intent vague/contradictory/insufficiently concrete for realisation; product underspecified/contradictory/insufficiently decomposable; requirements underspecified/contradictory/polluted by accidental implementation detail; or design incomplete/ambiguous/insufficiently operational for code. ADRs/design documents are load-bearing. Sufficiency depends on ambiguity governance; accepted relations may be reused only on exact basis after applicability/invalidation checks. A local selected function's span excludes rebuilding the whole product. The litmus neither waives the design profile's material-change gate nor requires recreation of unchanged accepted views.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed sufficiency, reconstruction-span and design-profile rules are externally owned.

grounding.quote:
The generative rule: a real use case (scenario, deployment, external review)
hits the current model; gap analysis identifies what the constitution cannot
express; if the gap is constitutional, not merely a missing implementation,
it re-enters at the layer its [change class](#change-classes) names, and
new goals or intent are written where it changes the work wave, direction
or scope; the repriced surface then flows forward through the layers that
class lists. New intents emerge from repeated, real use-case pressure
against the current model, not from abstract speculation; a gap becomes
intent only once it is concrete. Ad hoc coding pressure does not generate
intent; explicit gap analysis does. This is how the system stays alive
instead of becoming a frozen constitution.

constraints.statement: Explicit gap analysis identifies what the constitution cannot express. A constitutional gap, distinguished from missing implementation, re-enters at its change class's layer and flows forward through that class's layers. New goals/intent arise only where work-wave focus, direction or scope changes; intent emerges from concrete, repeated real-use pressure, not abstract speculation or ad hoc coding pressure. Requirements/design refine cumulatively, code is repeatedly re-derived, and implementation/testing/replay/scenario gaps feed repricing without reversing authority.
conditions: A real use case, including scenario, deployment or external review, pressures the current model.

grounding.quote:
Constitutional specification is current-surface law and is written in the
present tense. Dead law does not remain in active constitutional artifacts
for historical comfort: what is no longer live is deleted, superseded or
moved to commentary, and a migration wave does not justify preserving stale
constitutional wording inside the live surface (P3). During a change wave
the live constitutional surface is written in terms of the current truth
and the declared affected boundary; version-line branding such as `2.0` or
`3.0` is not used merely to indicate recency, and explicit version labels
are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings, or clearly
historical or superseded material (§6).

Before a downstream specification artifact is treated as complete, the
whole affected span is checked: is the change class clear; is the re-entry
point lawful for that class; can each downstream layer still be derived
from the upstream layer; do the active intent, product, requirements,
design and qualification surfaces still say the same thing in the affected
scope. If not, the gate is not closed (§4, consistency gate).

constraints.statement: Preserve each layer's role: goals do not replace requirements, intent excludes optional nonconstitutional implementation detail, product is not release notes, requirements carry explicit acceptance and material lifecycle obligations/gaps, and ADRs are not a second requirements surface. Live constitutional wording is present-tense current truth at its declared affected boundary; dead law is deleted, superseded or moved to commentary, even during migration. Recency alone does not justify version branding. Before treating a downstream artifact as complete, check the whole affected span for clear class, lawful re-entry, layer derivability and agreement among active intent/product/requirements/design/qualification; otherwise the gate stays open.
exceptions: Optional realisation detail may appear in intent when itself constitutional.
Explicit version labels are reserved for immutable release facts, selector bindings, or clearly historical/superseded material.

grounding.quote:
Requirements state what control or delivery surfaces must exist; design
decides the concrete mechanism that realises them. If a technology stack,
carrier or runtime is not already constrained by an upstream constitutional
surface, choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority
(P2, P1). A tenant's choice of stack, human process or
combination is its execution binding, declared in that design under §11.
The boundary matters especially for
agent-facing bootstrap and control surfaces: requirements may say that
authoritative bootstrap or control surfaces must be present, carry bare
axioms and route to the canonical method; design decides whether those
surfaces are entry documents, embedded blocks, standalone compiled
artifacts or another lawful topology (PRODUCT_DEFINITION §12). If
filenames and placement are hardcoded in requirements without
constitutional necessity, the requirement surface has absorbed design
detail and made re-derivation harder.

constraints.statement: Requirements specify required control/delivery surfaces; design chooses mechanisms, including stack/carrier/runtime and tenant execution binding unless upstream already constrains them. Agent-facing requirements may require authoritative bootstrap/control surfaces carrying bare axioms and routing to the canonical method; design chooses entry documents, embedded blocks, compiled artifacts or other lawful topology. Hardcoding filenames/placement without constitutional necessity absorbs design detail and impairs re-derivation.
exceptions: Upstream constitutional constraints bind choices; constitutional necessity may require specific filenames, placement, paths or packaging.

grounding.quote:
Non-goals of that profile (P1, P4a): it does not require one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
or replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type. It does require
that the implementation shape remain readable, modular and honest about
where meaning lives and where effects happen. Where a boundary composes
higher-order functions or effectful computation, it does require an
explicit composition and effect algebra with its applicable identity,
closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws (FOUNDATIONS
§4 Composition). The vocabulary is optional; the law is not.

constraints.statement: Semantic steps should read as transforms over admitted truth, with explicit effects pushed to the edge. Meaning requiring inspection of orchestration, mutable workspace state, service methods or fallback defaults indicates excessive imperative coupling. Readability, modularity and honesty about meaning/effects are required. A boundary composing higher-order functions or effectful computation requires explicit composition/effect algebra with applicable identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws.
constraints.uncertainty: The applicable algebra and profile-adoption rule are referenced but not fully supplied.
conditions: The design profile governs the realisation boundary.

grounding.quote:
Every inherited or legacy requirement is classified as one of these, and
nothing live remains unclassified (P3):

| Classification | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Deferred | retained in the live surface as an explicit not-yet-operative or not-yet-realised obligation | keep with an honest deferment surface; do not present as current closure |
| Superseded | ownership has moved to a newer constitutional surface or design decision | add Implements and Supersedes to the governing design record |
| Active | remains live constitutional law in the current surface | has an owning design decision; write or update one |
| Orphaned | no longer part of the intended system | remove or explicitly supersede |

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family has explicit header Status and Category; either missing makes it incomplete. All four categories remain constitutional, not priority or user-facing labels. Scenarios validate capability meaning; not every requirement should become a marketed feature. Requirements should avoid premature concrete realisation choices; nonconstitutional path/filename/packaging choices belong to design. Every inherited/legacy requirement is classified: Deferred remains explicitly not-yet-operative/realised with honest deferment and no current-closure claim; Superseded transfers ownership and requires Implements/Supersedes in its governing design record; Active requires an owning design decision to be written/updated; Orphaned is removed or explicitly superseded. Nothing live remains unclassified.

grounding.quote:
Ownership: every live requirement family maps to one or more owning design
decisions; every ADR or other design record grounds itself in requirements
through an explicit `Implements:` line.

Downstream closure: no live requirement remains a free-floating statement
of intent; if it is live it is realised through the downstream chain or
explicitly deferred with an honest surface that records the deferment, so
every live requirement family has downstream closure, realised in design,
code and tests or explicitly deferred. No shipping code or tests exist as
ungoverned behaviour: behaviour that exists traces back to live
requirements and the design decisions that authorise it. No hidden product
surface is allowed; behaviour without trace authority is accidental law
even if it works.

constraints.statement: Every live requirement family has one or more owning design decisions; every ADR/design record explicitly grounds requirements through Implements:. Live requirements close through design/code/tests or explicit honest deferment. All shipping code/tests trace to live requirements and authorising design; working untraced behaviour is still accidental law. Unowned requirements, ungrounded design, unrecorded deferment and ownerless code are drift; implementation-habit tests lock it in. Persistent event/projection delta is diagnosed by intake among code, requirement/design stack, predictive model or observation. Capability without a scenario has unverified operational meaning. Treating guarantees/governance/verification as features misclassifies them; in-place live-constitution correction corrupts history. A real-use gap inexpressible in requirements re-enters at Requirements or upstream according to class, not by a code hack.
exceptions: A live requirement may have an explicit honest deferment surface instead of realised design/code/tests.

grounding.quote:
Transitional implementation paths, migration
scaffolds and fallback behaviours have no permanent authority in the live
surface: once superseded they are retired, and any retained responsibility
satisfies the retention relation of §7 (closure criterion). The past is
preserved by version control, operational event history where present and
superseded constitutional artifacts. The method does not require shipping
compatibility shims forever, and it does not allow silent mutation of live
constitutional history.

constraints.statement: Published live constitutional domain artifacts cannot be silently mutated in place. An incorrect artifact is superseded by a new version or withdrawn/deleted from the live surface. Superseded transitions, scaffolds and fallbacks retire unless retention is justified; they have no permanent authority and compatibility shims need not ship forever. History is preserved by version control, operational events where present and superseded artifacts.
exceptions: Mutable implementation surfaces may be aggressively refactored while they retain that status.
Retained superseded responsibility must satisfy the migration retention relation.

grounding.quote:
For product definition this means naming the current product boundary,
intended use context, release and install posture, live-use posture,
observability posture, and retirement or supersession posture where those
materially affect the product's meaning. For requirements it means stating
any invariant obligation that governs build, assurance, release,
deployment, live usage, telemetry, retirement, ownership, source truth,
authority boundary or downstream interpretation; a requirement may defer a
phase only by naming the deferment and the surface that will own its later
resolution.

The rule is an ambiguity detector, not a demand that every requirement
become a release plan. Each phase has one of three answers, and this
section owns them: the phase is answered by the surface; if a phase is
not applicable, the surface says why; if it is unknown, a named gap such
as `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` is recorded.
Silent absence is not a valid lifecycle answer.
[ASSURANCE §16](ASSURANCE.md#16-module-lifecycle-confirmation) applies
the three answers to the design evidence of a governed boundary. When the lifecycle signal is
missing, downstream design may not fill the gap by local convention,
implementation precedent, prompt prose or test fixture; it reprices the
appropriate constitutional surface or carries the ambiguity as explicit,
governed debt (§5).

constraints.statement: Product names boundary, intended use, release/install, live-use, observability and retirement/supersession posture where material. Requirements state invariant build/assurance/release/deployment/use/telemetry/retirement/ownership/source-truth/authority/interpretation obligations. Product/requirements provide enough signal for design or explicitly record ambiguity. Deferral names both deferment and later resolution owner surface. Each phase is answered, reasoned not-applicable, or named unknown; silence is invalid. Missing signal requires constitutional repricing or explicit governed debt, never invention from convention, precedent, prompts or fixtures. These phase answers are declared states, map to no core value and cannot substitute for satisfied; consuming evaluation has its own predicate/result.
constraints.uncertainty: ASSURANCE §16 application and the full result calculus are not supplied.
conditions: Lifecycle aspects materially affect product meaning or an obligation.
exceptions: No implementation mechanism for every phase and no release plan for every requirement is demanded.

grounding.quote:
In the default scaffold `requirements/` is a folder under `specification/`.
Requirements may instead be stored at any location the product definition
binds, as individual files or grouped into requirement families. The default
shape exists to avoid collapsing the constitutional surface into one
monolithic requirements document, not to make folder placement
constitutional. This is one expression of the declarative bias: declaring
requirement structure and family boundaries is preferred over maintaining
one imperative catch-all document (P2).

allowed: Requirements at any location bound by Product Definition, as individual files or grouped requirement families.
Existing file layouts without moving or duplicating files merely to match conventional names.
forbidden: Treating conventional folder placement as constitutional authority.
Promoting a definition overlay or derived surface to co-equal WHAT authority.

grounding.quote:
Different designs may satisfy the same
requirements and different codebases the same design.

this litmus applies them to the method's own chain, where the span of a
local selected function excludes recreating the whole product. The design
profile owns design-view coverage, its material-change gate and
unchanged-boundary reuse; this litmus neither waives that gate nor requires
recreating unchanged accepted views ([DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md)).

allowed: Different designs may satisfy the same requirements and different codebases the same design.
Reuse an accepted relation on its exact basis after applicability and invalidation checks.
A selected local function need not reconstruct the whole product or unchanged accepted design views.
forbidden: Hiding major ambiguity to cross a boundary.
Waiving the applicable design-profile material-change gate.

grounding.quote:
If a technology stack,
carrier or runtime is not already constrained by an upstream constitutional
surface, choosing it is part of design, not a separate upstream authority
(P2, P1). A tenant's choice of stack, human process or
combination is its execution binding, declared in that design under §11.

allowed: Design chooses stack, carrier, runtime or human/mixed process where upstream constitutional law leaves it open.
Bootstrap/control topology may use entry documents, embedded blocks, standalone compiled artifacts or another lawful arrangement.
forbidden: Treating mechanism choice as a separate upstream authority.
Hardcoding mechanism detail in requirements without constitutional necessity.

grounding.quote:
Non-goals of that profile (P1, P4a): it does not require one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
or replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type. It does require
that the implementation shape remain readable, modular and honest about
where meaning lives and where effects happen. Where a boundary composes
higher-order functions or effectful computation, it does require an
explicit composition and effect algebra with its applicable identity,
closure, cardinality, effect and authority-conservation laws (FOUNDATIONS
§4 Composition). The vocabulary is optional; the law is not.

allowed: Not every exception needs a custom algebraic type.
forbidden: Using optional vocabulary as grounds to omit required composition/effect laws.
Obscuring meaning or effects at a governed boundary.

grounding.quote:
Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

residuals.uncertainty: F15 reports consumers in SPEC_METHOD, EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, WORLD_MODEL, ODD, IDENTITY, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, ACTIVATION, AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS, FOUNDATIONS, EVALUATION, TICKETS and CONFORMANCE, plus internal release clauses. It explicitly reports no separate consumer for external-dependency and support-line rows, and restricts operation-result consumers to this member; Product Definition maps its manager effects independently. Other reports include mandatory acceptance gates regardless of selected checks; digest-bound adopt versus selector-free sync; complete companion/dependency closure; unresolved successor disposition blocking acceptance; lifecycle, migration, commitment standing, repricing and work-carrier presence not supplying semantic disposition. Those external loci are not available to verify or expand.
residuals.consequence: The consumer list supplies reported directed applications, not independently verified governing edges to absent endpoints. Detailed consumer loci, numerical policy inventories and pillar assignments remain source-linked residual detail.

grounding.quote:
The table accounts for §1 to §3, §6 and §9 to §11. §1 Canonical statement
decides nothing of its own: each clause names its owning section. §8
binds the step of ACTIVATION to this method's terms; its delivery
priority is accounted for by family F5 at ACTIVATION §6, and the rest of
it by family F2 at ACTIVATION §1, whose paragraph after its table names
the rows §8 applies and the families that trace its statement of the
step's results and its use of the tenant's binding.

residuals.uncertainty: F10 reports consumers in ASSURANCE, DESIGN_MODULE, ODD, TICKETS, CONFORMANCE, WRITING_GUIDE, RELEASE, IDENTITY, PRODUCT_DEFINITION, POSTING_GUIDE, ACTIVATION and FOUNDATIONS plus internal method sections. Reports distinguish truth layers, trace every branch/test expectation, deny lifecycle labels admission/compliance/closure, apply inherited requirement status, bind execution as design, preserve present-tense/supersession, confirm lifecycle, deny ticket activity growth admission, keep posting distinct from adoption and execution kind distinct from operation kind. Evidence-closure and three-account mapping rows expressly have no separate consumer; their closure/evidence/refinement laws belong elsewhere. Exact category/status values, ADR defaults, lifecycle phases, progress categories, eight adoption steps, §11 details, discriminator contents, consumer loci and pillar associations are not fully represented or supplied as owning text.
residuals.consequence: Preserve the table's thirteen consequences and policy/owner distinctions as descriptions, without asserting external endpoint contents, executing account mappings, or proving derivations. Canonical statement adds no independent law; §8's step binding remains externally owned.

grounding.quote:
Reconstruction sufficiency depends on ambiguity governance (§5). The
hidden-ambiguity limit, reuse of an accepted relation's evidence, what
reconstructability requires and grants, and the reconstruction span are
stated once at
[EVALUATION §6 Layered sufficiency](EVALUATION.md#6-conformance-of-realisations);
this litmus applies them to the method's own chain, where the span of a
local selected function excludes recreating the whole product. The design
profile owns design-view coverage, its material-change gate and
unchanged-boundary reuse; this litmus neither waives that gate nor requires
recreating unchanged accepted views ([DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md)).

residuals.uncertainty: EVALUATION §6 and DESIGN_MODULE supply unprovided definitions, profile applicability, coverage, material-change and reuse predicates; P1/P2 foundations are cited but not established here.
residuals.consequence: Retain only the stated sufficiency, reuse and local-span boundaries; no complete reconstruction proof, profile adoption or design-view acceptance is inferred.
